title: Ownership (Part 2) - Immutable borrowing
learning_objectives: Use immutable borrows to inspect owned values without taking ownership.
Return one of multiple borrowed inputs without allocating a new owned value.
Recognize borrow-checker feedback when access rules conflict.
explanation: This ownership slice zooms in on immutable borrowing as an API design choice. When a function only needs to compare or inspect text, borrowing inputs and returning a borrowed result keeps ownership with the caller and avoids unnecessary allocation.

examples.title: Borrow a `String` to inspect it

compiler_error_examples: error[E0502]: cannot borrow as mutable because it is also borrowed as immutable
completion_criteria: Exercise tests pass without cloning either input string
Learner can explain why the returned label can be borrowed from one of the inputs
